steps.text: A lead sheet is a melody plus chord symbols — the whole song on one page. Jazz players read them; so can you. We'll sketch one as notes first; the score view (next to the piano roll) shows the same notes as notation.
steps.title: LEAD SHEETS

steps.text: Phrase one starts on C5, the tonic — home. Melodies that start home can wander freely, because the ear knows where home is.
steps.title: HOME

steps.text: D5 on step 3 — a step up. Singable melodies move mostly by step; leaps are spice, steps are the meal.
steps.title: STEP UP

steps.text: G5 on step 5 — a leap of a fourth. After a leap, melodies usually step back down; the ear wants the balance restored.
steps.title: LEAP

steps.text: Finish the phrase: bring it home. Add E5 (76) on step 6 and C5 (72) on step 8. Two steps down, landing on the tonic — resolution you can feel.
steps.title: RESOLVE

steps.text: That's a lead-sheet melody: home, wander, leap, resolve. Write the chord symbols above it (C, F, G…) and a player can perform your song from this alone.
steps.title: DONE

title: Writing a lead sheet in the score view
